text:
ella: weird CI failure on macOS runner: tests that spin up FastAPI + uvicorn + httpx.AsyncClient are throwing `RuntimeError: There is no current event loop in thread 'Thread-1'`.

ella: reproduction is flaky locally but consistently failing on mac-latest in CI.

sam: are we using uvloop or custom loop policy in our tests or sampleapp?

ella: sampleapp doesn't explicitly set anything. but some infra scripts call `asyncio.set_event_loop_policy(uvloop.EventLoopPolicy())` in test bootstrap for perf.

morgan: that rings a bell. uvloop on mac can behave differently w/ threads. AsyncClient uses asyncio.get_running_loop() internally sometimes and that breaks if the loop policy creates non-default loop types across threads.

ella: minimal snippet I used:
```py
# tests/conftest.py
import asyncio
import uvloop

asyncio.set_event_loop_policy(uvloop.EventLoopPolicy())

# test spins up TestClient(app) which spawns uvicorn in thread
```

ella: then inside app startup we do `client = AsyncClient()` and `asyncio.create_task(_keepalive(client))`.

sam: create_task on a background thread where uvicorn started will fail if the current thread has no running loop. create_task delegates to the event loop of the current thread.

morgan: quick suggestion: in frameworks spawn path, prefer `loop = asyncio.get_running_loop(); loop.create_task(...)` inside async startup. But if startup runs in a thread with a different policy it may still be problematic.

ella: I tried switching the test bootstrap to call `uvloop.install()` instead of set_event_loop_policy, and CI improved but not consistent.

infra-bot: FYI, mac-latest runner uses Python 3.11 and has a different thread model for the default loop. See https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-policy.html#event-loop-policies .

ella: one hack that stabilized things locally: create AsyncClient in startup and stash on app.state, and use `anyio.from_thread.run` wrapper when starting tasks from sync contexts. But that's not great as a docs-only fix.

sam: Could we add an SDK helper that hides this complexity? e.g. in sdk-python: `sdk.http.provide_app_client(app, uvloop_compatible=False)` that wires proper install/teardown and offers `create_background_task(coro)` that uses the running loop safely.

morgan: +1. Also important to document: do not call `asyncio.set_event_loop_policy` at import time in tests, prefer configuring per-worker or in a pytest fixture that runs before the app starts.

ella: I filed an issue with repro & logs: https://git.internal/redwood/devex/issues/902 - includes a tiny dockerized test runner that reproduces on mac and linux.

qa-bot: attached CI failure: https://ci.internal/20002/failed-log.txt showing `RuntimeError` at httpx/_utils.py:112.

sam: for immediate mitigation, add a lint in sampleapp tests that disallows top-level set_event_loop_policy usage and warn in the template README. We can follow up with an SDK helper.

ella: I'll open a PR to update the sampleapp and add a test that explicitly runs with uvloop policy in a fixture to catch regressions.

morgan: filed SDK issue too: https://git.internal/redwood/sdk-python/issues/411 - proposes `LifecycleAsyncClient` + `attach_task` helpers. Marking good-first-pr.

ella: thanks, folks. saving this thread for the follow-up docs update. :white_check_mark:
